Plot glex Variable Importances

Source: R/plot.R
plot.glex_vi.Rd

Plot glex Variable Importances

Usage

# S3 method for class 'glex_vi'
plot(
  x,
  by_degree = FALSE,
  threshold = NULL,
  max_interaction = NULL,
  scale = "absolute",
  ...
)

Arguments

x

Object of class glex_vi, see glex_vi().

by_degree

(logical(1): FALSE) Optionally sum values by degree of interaction, resulting in one contribution score for all main effects, all second-order interactions, etc.

threshold

(numeric(1): NULL) Terms with an importance score at or below this are aggregated under a "Remaining terms" label. Refers to the chosen scale (and the measure of the glex_vi() object). The default NULL uses 2.5% of the largest score (per class for multiclass objects), so negligible terms do not crowd the plot, and 0 with by_degree = TRUE. Set 0 to show all terms.

max_interaction

(integer(1): NULL) Optionally filter plot to show terms up to the specified degree of interaction. Similar to threshold, all other terms will be aggregated under a "Remaining terms" label.

scale

("absolute") Plot m (default) or m_rel ("relative") of glex_vi(): for its default measure = "mean_abs", the average absolute contributions or the same value scaled by the average prediction; for "variance", the mean square or its share of the variance of the prediction; for "share", the pruning's share either way.

...

(Unused)

Value

A ggplot object.

See also

glex_vi

Other Visualization functions: plot.glex(), plot_force(), plot_pdp(), plot_shap_decomposition(), plot_waterfall()

Examples

library(xgboost)
x <- as.matrix(mtcars[, -1])
xg <- xgboost(x, mtcars$mpg, max_depth = 3, nrounds = 10, nthreads = 1)
vi <- glex_vi(glex(xg, x))

plot(vi, threshold = 0.05)

plot(vi, by_degree = TRUE)
